text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:

- Swiss banks matched 11 heirs to unclaimed funds locked in Swiss bank accounts, the Swiss banking ombudsman said as he presented an intermediate report on the issue. The sum of their unclaimed funds amounted to 1.6 million Swiss francs. Some 11,000 Swiss francs belong to heirs of Holocaust victims. In a first reaction, the Jewish World Congress said that the result was pathetic. U.S. Senator D'Amato plans to wite a letter to the obudsman demanding complete access to the archives for an independent commission.

- Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti met German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel in Bonn to discuss Switzerland's integration into Europe. At a news conference, Cotti said that without Germany's help, Switzerland would not have received the same attention during bilateral negotiations between Switzerland and the European Union.

- Investigations of the murder of a Swiss peace corps worker in Madagascar will be expanded to Switzerland as two Madagascan officials will question three colleagues of the victim who are in Switzerland. The three are suspected to be involved in an corruption scandal.
- Poverty in Switzerland is rising. Within four years, the number of people who needed financial support from social security insitutions doubled to 300,000 people, according to a study.
